content: 1. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Cobicistat also increases rimegepant levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by reducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Cobicistat similarly increases riociguat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If used, monitor for hypotension and adjust the dose as needed. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir and cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir has a similar effect. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID if platelet counts are ≥100 x 10^9/L. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. 7. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of salmeterol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 8. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its prescribing information. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with CYP2C9 inhibitors. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sofpironium topical by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Darunavir and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration or interrupt sparsentan treatment if unavoidable. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration as suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tadalafil dosage for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) or erectile dysfunction (ED) as per specific recommendations. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting BCRP transport. Monitor for adverse reactions if coadministration is unavoidable. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its conversion to active metabolites. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration as ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or monitor for loss of efficacy. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it before the next infusion. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates as per product labeling. 36. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 42. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If adverse effects occur, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Darunavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for hyperglycemia or diabetes exacerbation. 49. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 50. Darunavir decreases the effects of albiglutide due to insulin resistance. Monitor for hyperglycemia. 51. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 52. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 53. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for antiarrhythmic effects. 54. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Carefully titrate antidepressant doses to achieve the desired effect. 55. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. 56. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 57. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amoxapine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate antidepressant doses to achieve the desired effect. 58. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 59. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 60. Aprepitant increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 61. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25–50% when coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. 62. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 63. Cobicistat and darunavir may alter the efficacy of artemether/lumefantrine. Monitor for QT prolongation and reduced antimalarial efficacy. 64. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for immune reconstitution syndrome. 65. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the atogepant dose to 10 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 66. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust atorvastatin dose as per recommendations. 67. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the avatrombopag dose when treating ITP as per the drug monograph. 68. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 69. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy as needed. 70. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for respiratory depression. 71. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of berotralstat by inhibiting BCRP transport. Monitor for adverse effects. 72. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of betrixaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Adjust the betrixaban dose as per recommendations. 73. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 74. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust bosentan dose as per recommendations. 75. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 76. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse effects.
